body:
The Gaussian block proof rounds to the p-grid and then asserts an error bound that can be smaller than any possible grid error. For the exact scalar value h/2, with P=p+12 and unit chirp factors, the asserted bound is h/8, whereas every p-grid value is at distance at least h/2.

Label that bound as the internal, pre-extraction enclosure and account separately for the <sqrt(2)h complex component-truncation error. Retain the fine dyadic block value until the S' normalization or E subtraction is complete. Exact rational normalization followed by fine-grid truncation preserves the existing <3h forward and <5h correction-map budgets, under the other estimates used in the source proof. The stated output allowances and asymptotic cost are unchanged.

The rounding defect and counterexample were identified by GPT-6 Pro. Codex independently confirmed the exact arithmetic and propagated the correction through these two calculations. Existing eumemic/icekylinx and Harvey–van der Hoeven attribution is retained. This is an AI-generated and AI-reviewed correction, with no human or formal verification claimed. It does not supply a new multiplication exponent or verify the inherited analytic/source hypotheses.

The correction is conditional on the parameter bounds already used in the chirp calculations, including theta<=1/4 and sigma<2. The referenced no-sort lemma header is broader; this patch does not resolve that inherited domain mismatch or certify the containing lemma at its full printed scope.

Validation: the independent exact counterexample already passed the pinned local runner. The added small standard-library checker verifies the scalar witness and rational endpoint budgets. Exact replay, patch-application, and immutable source receipts accompany the review packet.
title: Account for final-grid rounding in the Gaussian block enclosure
